code:
x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
np.var(x)            # 1.25   -- numpy default: ddof=0
np.var(x, ddof=1)    # 1.667  -- sample version
pd.Series(x).var()   # 1.667  -- pandas default: ddof=1
caption: numpy divides by n unless told otherwise; pandas divides by n-1 by default.

eyebrow: Why n-1: Bessel's correction, by simulation
code:
data = rng.normal(loc=0, scale=10, size=(100000, 5))   # true variance = 100
data.var(axis=1, ddof=0).mean()   # ~80.2  -- divide by n: too low
data.var(axis=1, ddof=1).mean()   # ~100.3 -- divide by n-1: right on target
caption: A sample sits closer to its own mean than the true one — dividing by n underestimates spread.
